images.note: Beat: Box 1 — 'one in five industrial workers were kids' (nearly 18% under 16, 1900). Lewis Hine photograph of a Paterson, New Jersey textile mill (National Child Labor Committee work). 2500x1797, 2MB. ICP's object page (accession 891.1975) carries no creation date; Hine's Paterson mill series was made for the NCLC ca. 1908-1909 — contemporary to the beat. Viewed to confirm subject. Alt: none qualifying — the obvious LOC Hine spinner/breaker-boy scans cap at ~1024px wide (failing the 1200px gate); NYPL blocked (Incapsula), George Eastman Museum 403, UMBC unreachable; no second institutional source found at bar.
images.source: International Center of Photography (Lewis Hine, Paterson NJ textiles, acc. 891.1975)
images.title: Child workers in a Paterson, New Jersey textile mill (Lewis Hine, ca. 1908)

images.note: Beat: Box 2 — Knights of Labor under Terence Powderly (secretive, anyone-except-lawyers-and-bankers, 700,000 by 1886) vs Gompers's AFL. Engraved frontispiece portrait of T. V. Powderly in profile, signed 'Sincerely Yours, T. V. Powderly,' from his own 'Thirty Years of Labor' (1890) — fully contemporary (he led the Knights 1879-1893). 2358x3542, 1.1MB. Viewed to confirm subject. Alt: none qualifying — the LOC 'Leaders of the Knights of Labor' lithograph scans at only 822x1024px; Digital Commonwealth has no Powderly portrait; Chicago History Museum 403; no second institutional source at bar.
images.source: Internet Archive (Thirty Years of Labor, 1859-1889, published 1890)
images.title: Terence V. Powderly, Grand Master Workman of the Knights of Labor (1890 engraving)

images.note: Beat: Box 3 — Haymarket, May 4, 1886: anarchist rally, police march in, bomb kills seven officers, eight anarchists tried. Contemporary Harper's Weekly engraving 'The Anarchist Riot in Chicago — A Dynamite Bomb Exploding Among the Police' (May 15, 1886, eleven days after the bombing). 8226x11748, 3.5MB. Leaf located via OCR leaf-mapping on leaf n7. Alt: none qualifying — Chicago History Museum images 403, HathiTrust catalog API 403; no second institutional source for this engraving at bar.
images.source: Internet Archive — Harper's Weekly, May 15, 1886 (Harper & Brothers)
images.title: The Haymarket bombing, Chicago, May 4, 1886 (contemporary engraving)

images.note: Beat: Box 3 — Homestead, July 1892: Frick, lockout, 300 Pinkertons by barge at dawn, day-long battle, Pinkertons surrender and run the gauntlet, workers retake the plant, then 8,000 state militiamen retake it. Cover of Harper's Weekly, July 16, 1892 (ten days after the battle): 'THE HOMESTEAD RIOT — Drawn by W. P. Snyder after a Photograph by Dabbs, Pittsburg. THE PINKERTON MEN LEAVING THE BARGES AFTER THE SURRENDER.' 4008x6056, 2.1MB. Viewed to confirm subject. Alt: none qualifying — Digital Library of Georgia search is JS-only (no API path found), Historic Pittsburgh behind Cloudflare, Newberry search 404; no second institutional source at bar.
images.source: Internet Archive — Harper's Weekly, July 16, 1892, cover (Harper & Brothers)
images.title: The Homestead Riot — Pinkerton men leaving the barges after the surrender (July 1892)

images.note: Beat: Box 3 — Eugene Debs, American Railway Union, the Pullman boycott ('a boycott that paralyzed the whole rail system'), jailed, 'came out a socialist.' Photogravure frontispiece portrait of Eugene V. Debs, signed 'Your comrade, Eugene V. Debs,' from 'Debs: His Life, Writings and Speeches' (1908) — 14 years after Pullman, from his own movement's press (Appeal to Reason). 1515x2462, 212KB. Viewed to confirm subject. Alt: none qualifying — Boston Public Library/Digital Commonwealth 'Eugene Debs' photo (ca. 1920-1926) serves via chunked IIIF with no Content-Length (fails the verification bar); Indiana State Debs collection unreachable; no second institutional source at bar.
images.source: Internet Archive (Debs: His Life, Writings and Speeches, 1908)
images.title: Eugene V. Debs (photogravure frontispiece, 1908)

images.note: Beat: Box 3 — Pullman, 1894: company town, rent, ARU boycott, federal troops, ~25 strikers killed, Debs jailed. Cover of Harper's Weekly, July 14, 1894, at the strike's peak: W. A. Rogers's 'KING DEBS' cartoon — Debs crowned 'American Railway Union' straddling the 'Highway of Trade' amid closed depots, 'Pullman Sleeper,' and 'No Freight Received' signs. The single best contemporary visual of the boycott paralyzing the rail system. 3784x5608, 1.5MB. Viewed to confirm subject. Alt: none — no second institutional source for this cartoon at bar.
images.source: Internet Archive — Harper's Weekly, July 14, 1894, cover (Harper & Brothers)
images.title: 'King Debs' — the Pullman boycott paralyzes the railroads (July 1894 cartoon)
